niche: a Spanish home-workout subscription app placing each paid acquisition channel of its 2027 media plan in the growth policy's scale, hold or cut band, on the 12-month net revenue per euro that the plan's weekly spend on the channel buys
answer: scale Google iOS and Pinterest iOS; hold Meta iOS, Google Android and AppLovin Android; cut TikTok iOS and Snapchat iOS (2027 return per euro at the plan's weekly spend, from generator/core.py: Pinterest iOS 1.66, Google iOS 1.43; Meta iOS 1.07, Google Android 1.04, AppLovin Android 1.03; Snapchat iOS 0.64, TikTok iOS 0.61); three stumps on three axes, three open channels each opened by its own stump, seven distinct wrong calls across the lattice
answer_source: task1/generator/core.py at the draw; task1/generator/figures.json once the pack is cut
analyst_test: A careful but hurried analyst trues the app's billing records up to the stores' reports month by month (each recorded charge scaled by its store-month's ratio), prices every install postback of an iOS network at the value its consenting installs showed at the same first two days, and fits installs and value per install on each week's spend; that route cuts AppLovin Android and Google Android and scales Meta iOS, against the golden's hold on all three, and files every other channel's return 19 to 43 per cent off.
domain_test: Each result is an acquisition-economics and lifetime-value quantity of a subscription app (the store charges the app's records never took in, an install's 12-month net revenue where the attribution export holds no channel, what a weekly budget buys in an auction, the return per euro at a plan's spend and what the next euro returns); swap the nouns for another field's and the store reports, the tracking prompt, the install postbacks and the ad auction stop making sense.
layer1: attribution rows re-sent after an SDK retry
staff and test accounts with sandbox charges
store report rows on the stores' own day boundaries
install postbacks dated three or four days after the install
refunds in the stores' reports and the billing records
reinstalls on a second device under one account
the networks' own install counts crediting view-throughs
stakeholder_role: the head of financial planning, who signs the 2027 insertion orders with the ad networks in December

world.org_type: a home-workout and yoga subscription app

driver: Each channel's band rests on what a euro of its 2027 spend returns in twelve months, a quantity no record holds: the app's billing records hold a store charge only once the subscriber next opens the app, the attribution export holds an iOS network's installs only where the user allowed tracking (and those users are worth more than the rest at the same first two days), and a week's spend is what the ad platform delivered of the week's budget given that week's auction, so each part of the return is estimated from the record that sees it and checked on a slice where it is known (the web checkout's subscribers, the one network whose channel is on every account, the weeks the team moved a budget).
driver_concrete: Zancada's growth policy places a paid channel in scale, hold or cut on its 12-month net revenue per euro at the 2027 plan's weekly spend (1.20 and 0.90 the lines). Subscribers who stop opening the app keep paying and the records take in none of it (12 to 35 per cent of a channel's twelve-month revenue, most on AppLovin Android); about 28 per cent of an iOS network's installs allowed tracking and they are worth about twice the rest, the rest sitting among the accounts with no channel; and installs rise about one for one with a week's spend in the record while a budget buys them at an elasticity of 0.66 to 0.82, because the platform spends more of a budget in the weeks its auction is cheap.
stump: The careful but hurried route (records trued up to the stores' totals month by month, every postback at the consenting installs' value by first-48-hour value, the response fitted on spend) cuts AppLovin Android (0.74) and Google Android (0.80) and scales Meta iOS (1.35) against the golden's three holds; each stump dropped alone flips its own channel and no stump fixed alone reaches the call.
results: R1 the share of each channel's 12-month net revenue the app's billing records never took in; R2 each iOS network's 12-month net revenue per install over every install it bought; R3 what a week's budget buys on each channel (installs and their value) and what the next euro returns at the plan's spend; R4 each channel's 2027 return per euro and net revenue per install at the plan's weekly spend; R5 the same return at the plan's stretch spend; R6 the plan's 12-month net revenue on the iOS networks and what the stretch spend adds; R7 each channel's band
one_fact_test: the most useful sentence (the stores' excess over the records belongs to subscriptions last seen still set to renew whose owners stopped opening the app) leaves the candidates, the trial-end share and the continuation to fit, rescues R1 alone on the reflex route (1 of 7) and 5 rubric points; the consent sentence and the budget sentence rescue no whole result

differentiation.mark115: mark115 forecast a deal mechanic's second response where its new level crosses a rival's, measured on the stores that moved; here no response at a rival's level decides anything: each channel's 12-month return is estimated from three records with their own blind spots (store charges the app sees only at the subscriber's next open, iOS installs the attribution export sees only with tracking consent, a weekly spend the auction sets), each opening a different channel and each ruled on by a slice the plan's channels do not reach
